To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an EM-guided feeding tube that perforates the oesophagus may not be detected by the EM signal or by plain chest X-ray and should be confirmed by CT following injection of radiocontrast medium down the feeding tube.
the EM trace is not reliable for detecting oesophageal tube perforation or misplacement.

the development and application of a new type of non-intrusive sensor for monitoring and diagnosis of the human body.
the use of a new type of EM guidance to help the clinician in placing a feeding tube in the stomach.
the development of a system for the detection and localization of oesophageally placed feeding tubes.

the EM trace is not a reliable guide to the correct positioning of a feeding tube in the oesophagus.
the Cortrak system is a safe, reliable and effective device for the safe and accurate placement of feeding tubes.
EM guidance is not an adequate method of detecting oesophageal tube perforation, and should not be used as the sole means of verifying tube position in high-risk patients.
